title: Second-Order Actor-Critic Methods for Discounted MDPs via Policy Hessian Decomposition
comments: 9 pages, 2 figures including Appendix with Detailed proofs
summary: We address the discounted reward setting in reinforcement learning (RL). To mitigate the value approximation challenges in policy gradient methods, actor-critic approaches have been developed and are known to converge to stationary points under suitable assumptions. However, these methods rely on first-order updates. In contrast, second-order optimization provides principled curvature-aware updates that are proven to accelerate convergence, but its application in RL is limited by the computational complexity of Hessian estimation. In this work, we analyze second-order approximations for the actor update that leverage the full curvature information of the objective as much as possible. A stable approximation requires treating the action-value function as locally constant with respect to policy parameters, which does not generally hold in policy gradient methods. We show that this approximation becomes well-justified under a two-timescale actor-critic framework, where the critic evolves on a faster timescale and can be treated as quasi-stationary during actor updates. Building on this insight, we formulate a second-order actor-critic method for the discounted reward setting that leverages Hessian-vector product (HVP) computations, resulting in a computationally efficient and stable second-order update.
comment: 9 pages, 2 figures including Appendix with Detailed proofs

title: MasFACT: Continual Multi-Agent Topology Learning via Geometry-Aware Posterior Transfer
summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) powered by large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a powerful paradigm for complex problem solving, where performance critically depends on the underlying inter-agent communication topology. However, existing topology generation methods mainly optimize for isolated tasks, while real-world deployments involve streams of evolving tasks, requiring previously effective collaboration patterns to be retained and reused rather than rediscovered or overwritten. We identify a previously underexplored failure mode, \emph{topology forgetting}, in which adapting to new tasks shifts the topology generator away from communication structures required by earlier tasks. This issue stems from cross-task misalignment in both agent-level functional semantics and relational communication structures. To address this challenge, we propose \textbf{\textsc{MasFACT}}, a geometry-aware posterior transfer framework that preserves and reuses historical collaboration knowledge as transferable topology priors. We transfer these priors across task-specific agent spaces through Fused Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport and perform PAC-Bayes-guided conservative posterior adaptation to balance task-specific plasticity with structural stability. Experiments across class-, domain-, and task-level continual settings demonstrate that \textsc{MasFACT} consistently improves average accuracy while reducing topology forgetting compared to strong topology generation and replay-based baselines, and can be seamlessly integrated with different MAS topology generators.

AI.title_translation: MasFACT：通过几何感知后验迁移的持续多智能体拓扑学习
AI.tldr: 本文提出了MasFACT框架，通过最优传输和PAC-Bayes指导的后验适应，解决了多智能体系统在持续任务学习中的“拓扑遗忘”问题，实现了协作拓扑知识的跨任务保留与复用。
AI.motivation: 现有的多智能体系统（MAS）拓扑生成方法主要针对孤立任务进行优化，而在实际应用的任务流中，需要保留和复用先前有效的协作模式。然而，适应新任务会导致拓扑生成器偏离先前任务所需的通信结构，产生“拓扑遗忘”问题，这主要是由于跨任务在智能体级功能语义和关系通信结构上的不对齐导致的。
AI.method: 提出MasFACT框架，这是一种几何感知的后验迁移框架。该框架将历史协作知识保留为可迁移的拓扑先验，通过融合Gromov-Wasserstein（Fused Gromov-Wasserstein）最优传输在任务特定的智能体空间之间迁移这些先验，并执行基于PAC-Bayes指导的保守后验适应，以在任务特定的可塑性与结构稳定性之间取得平衡。
AI.result: 在类别、领域和任务级别的持续学习设置下的实验表明，与强拓扑生成和基于重放的基线方法相比，MasFACT在持续提高平均准确率的同时，显著减少了拓扑遗忘，并且可以无缝集成到不同的MAS拓扑生成器中。
AI.conclusion: MasFACT能够有效缓解多智能体系统在持续学习过程中的拓扑遗忘问题，在保持历史协作结构稳定性的同时兼顾了新任务的可塑性，为动态多智能体协作提供了高效且鲁棒的解决方案。
AI.translation: 由大语言模型（LLM）驱动的多智能体系统（MAS）已成为解决复杂问题的一种强大范式，其性能在很大程度上取决于底层的智能体间通信拓扑。然而，现有的拓扑生成方法主要针对孤立的任务进行优化，而现实世界的部署涉及不断演化的任务流，这需要保留和复用以前有效的协作模式，而不是重新发现或覆盖它们。我们发现了一种以前未被充分探索的失效模式，即“拓扑遗忘”，即适应新任务会使拓扑生成器偏离早期任务所需的通信结构。这一问题源于跨任务在智能体级功能语义和关系通信结构上的不对齐。为了应对这一挑战，我们提出了 MasFACT，一个几何感知的后验迁移框架，该框架将历史协作知识保留并复用为可迁移的拓扑先验。我们通过融合 Gromov-Wasserstein 最优传输在特定任务的智能体空间之间迁移这些先验，并进行 PAC-Bayes 指导的保守后验适应，以平衡特定任务的可塑性与结构稳定性。在类别、领域和任务级别的持续设置中的实验表明，与强大的拓扑生成和基于重放的基线相比，MasFACT 在减少拓扑遗忘的同时，持续提高了平均准确率，并且可以与不同的 MAS 拓扑生成器无缝集成。
AI.summary: 本文针对大语言模型驱动的多智能体系统在面对持续演化任务时出现的“拓扑遗忘”问题，提出了MasFACT框架。该框架通过融合Gromov-Wasserstein最优传输和PAC-Bayes指导的后验适应，将历史协作知识作为可迁移的拓扑先验进行复用，从而在维持结构稳定性的同时实现了高效的新任务拓扑学习。
AI.keywords: 多智能体系统, 拓扑学习, 持续学习, 拓扑遗忘, 最优传输
AI.comments: 该论文首次识别并定义了多智能体持续拓扑学习中的“拓扑遗忘”这一关键问题。其创新之处在于引入了几何感知的后验迁移框架，巧妙地结合了融合Gromov-Wasserstein最优传输（解决跨任务空间不一致的对齐问题）与PAC-Bayes理论（平衡稳定性与可塑性）。该方法不仅具有扎实的理论基础，而且能够无缝集成到现有的多种MAS拓扑生成器中，对于推动多智能体系统在动态、持续演化场景下的实际落地具有重要价值。

title: CriterAlign: Criterion-Centric Rationale Alignment for Code Preference Judging
summary: Pairwise human preference prediction is central to evaluating code-generation systems, where quality often depends on task-specific trade-offs beyond functional correctness. While rubric-based LLM judges improve interpretability by decomposing evaluation into explicit criteria, most existing pipelines remain pointwise: they score each response independently and derive preferences by comparing aggregated scores. We show that this design is poorly matched to pairwise code preference prediction and can underperform a strong monolithic judge. We propose CriterAlign, a criterion-centric framework that adapts rubric-based judging to pairwise preference evaluation through direct criterion-level pairwise judgments, tie-driven criterion refinement, swap-consistency filtering, and final pairwise synthesis. We further introduce Human-Preference-Aligned Guidance (HPAG), synthesized offline from training examples by extracting recurring rationale gaps between human preferences and monolithic judge predictions, and injected into the criterion generator, criterion judge, and final judge. On BigCodeReward, CriterAlign improves a Qwen2.5-VL-32B monolithic judge from 60.4% to 66.3% accuracy, with ablations confirming the contributions of pairwise criterion design and HPAG.

AI.title_translation: CriterAlign: 以准则为中心的理由对齐用于代码偏好判断
AI.tldr: 现有基于规则的LLM代码偏好评判是点对点的且表现不佳。CriterAlign引入了一个以准则为中心的成对评判框架，并结合人类偏好对齐指导（HPAG），显著提高了代码偏好预测的准确性。
AI.motivation: 成对的人类偏好预测是评估代码生成系统的核心，但现有基于规则的LLM评判大多是点对点的，导致其在成对代码偏好预测中表现不佳，甚至不如强大的整体评判。代码质量往往取决于超越功能正确性的任务特定权衡。
AI.method: CriterAlign是一个以准则为中心的框架，通过直接的准则级别成对判断、平局驱动的准则细化、交换一致性过滤和最终的成对合成，将基于规则的评判适应成对偏好评估。此外，它引入了人类偏好对齐指导（HPAG），通过提取人类偏好与整体评判预测之间反复出现的理由差距，从训练样本中离线合成，并注入到准则生成器、准则评判和最终评判中。
AI.result: 在BigCodeReward上，CriterAlign将Qwen2.5-VL-32B整体评判的准确率从60.4%提高到66.3%。消融实验证实了成对准则设计和HPAG的贡献。
AI.conclusion: CriterAlign通过其以准则为中心的成对设计和HPAG，有效解决了点对点基于规则的LLM评判的局限性，显著提高了代码偏好预测的准确性。
AI.translation: 成对的人类偏好预测是评估代码生成系统的核心，其中质量通常取决于超越功能正确性的任务特定权衡。虽然基于规则的LLM评判通过将评估分解为明确的标准来提高可解释性，但大多数现有流程仍然是点对点的：它们独立地对每个响应进行评分并通过比较聚合分数来得出偏好。我们表明这种设计与成对的代码偏好预测不匹配，并且可能不如强大的整体评判。我们提出了CriterAlign，一个以准则为中心的框架，通过直接的准则级别成对判断、平局驱动的准则细化、交换一致性过滤和最终的成对合成，使基于规则的评判适应成对偏好评估。我们进一步引入了人类偏好对齐指导（HPAG），通过提取人类偏好与整体评判预测之间反复出现的理由差距，从训练样本中离线合成，并注入到准则生成器、准则评判和最终评判中。在BigCodeReward上，CriterAlign将Qwen2.5-VL-32B整体评判的准确率从60.4%提高到66.3%，消融实验证实了成对准则设计和HPAG的贡献。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了CriterAlign，一个用于代码生成评估中成对人类偏好预测的新型以准则为中心的框架。它通过整合直接的准则级别成对判断、细化、过滤和合成，解决了现有基于规则的点对点LLM评判的缺点。此外，它提出了人类偏好对齐指导（HPAG），以弥合人类偏好与整体评判预测之间的差距。在BigCodeReward上的实验表明，CriterAlign显著提高了LLM评判在代码偏好方面的准确性。
AI.keywords: 代码偏好判断, 理由对齐, LLM评判, 成对评估, 人类偏好
AI.comments: CriterAlign的创新之处在于将代码偏好评估从点对点转向成对的、以准则为中心的方法，这更符合比较性任务的本质。引入HPAG以明确与人类理由对齐，解决了LLM评估中常见的挑战，这尤其重要。这项工作有望显著提高自动化代码质量评估的可靠性和可解释性。

title: MAVEN: A Multi-stage Agentic Annotation Pipeline for Video Reasoning Tasks
summary: Training Vision Language Models (VLMs) for video event reasoning requires high-quality structured annotations capturing not only what happened, but when, where, why, and with what consequence, at a scale manual labelling cannot support. We present MAVEN (Multi-stage Agentic Video Event aNnotation), a multi-stage agentic pipeline that turns raw videos into multi-task training data with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning traces, organized around a designated Event of Focus. At its core, MAVEN synthesizes a Multi-Scale Spatio-Temporal Event Description (MSTED) from three complementary caption levels; this explicit intermediate serves as the sole input to downstream Q&A generation across multiple task formats. Crucially, MAVEN supports agent-driven domain adaptation: given a new video dataset and target question examples, the agent redesigns all prompts top-down without manual re-engineering. A hierarchical refinement loop further classifies annotation errors against a taxonomy, traces root causes to the originating pipeline stage, and applies targeted edits that rewrite prompts or modify the pipeline structure itself, iteratively improving data quality. We apply MAVEN to label over 5,300 traffic videos and fine-tune Cosmos-Reason2-8B on the resulting data. On a private CCTV evaluation set, fine-tuning surpasses both Gemini 2.5 Pro and 3.1 Flash, including a $+38.8$-point gain in MCQ accuracy over zero-shot. On AccidentBench, CCTV-only training lifts Cosmos-Reason2 by $+10.7$ MCQ points and matches Gemini 2.5 Pro despite seeing no dashcam videos; adding agent-adapted dashcam annotations narrows the gap to Gemini 3.1 Flash, and RL post-training pushes overall performance past both Gemini baselines. Qualitative results on warehouse surveillance and public safety videos further show the agentic workflow readily adapts the pipeline to new domains.

AI.title_translation: MAVEN：用于视频推理任务的多阶段智能体标注流程
AI.tldr: MAVEN是一个多阶段智能体标注流程，能将原始视频转化为高质量的多任务训练数据，并通过智能体驱动的领域适应和分层优化循环，显著提升视频推理任务中大型视觉语言模型的性能，超越了Gemini 2.5 Pro和3.1 Flash。
AI.motivation: 训练用于视频事件推理的视觉语言模型（VLMs）需要高质量、结构化的标注数据，不仅要捕捉事件内容，还要包括时间、地点、原因和结果。然而，手动标注无法支持所需的数据规模。
AI.method: MAVEN（Multi-stage Agentic Video Event aNnotation）是一个多阶段智能体标注流程。它将原始视频转化为带有思维链（CoT）推理轨迹的多任务训练数据，并围绕一个指定的焦点事件进行组织。其核心是合成一个多尺度时空事件描述（MSTED），该描述由三个互补的字幕级别生成，并作为下游问答生成的唯一输入。MAVEN支持智能体驱动的领域适应，可以根据新的视频数据集和目标问题示例，自动重新设计提示。一个分层优化循环会识别标注错误，追溯根本原因，并应用有针对性的编辑来重写提示或修改流程结构，从而迭代地提高数据质量。
AI.result: MAVEN被用于标注超过5,300个交通视频，并用生成的数据微调了Cosmos-Reason2-8B。在私有CCTV评估集上，微调后的模型超越了Gemini 2.5 Pro和3.1 Flash，其中MCQ准确率比零样本提高了+38.8点。在AccidentBench上，仅CCTV训练使Cosmos-Reason2的MCQ得分提高了+10.7点，并与Gemini 2.5 Pro持平。添加智能体适应的行车记录仪标注缩小了与Gemini 3.1 Flash的差距，并且RL后训练使总体性能超越了两个Gemini基线。在仓库监控和公共安全视频上的定性结果表明，智能体工作流可以很容易地将流程适应到新领域。
AI.conclusion: MAVEN通过其多阶段智能体标注流程、MSTED生成、智能体驱动的领域适应和分层优化循环，能够高效地生成高质量的视频推理训练数据，并显著提升了大型视觉语言模型在视频推理任务上的表现，超越了现有SOTA模型。
AI.translation: 训练用于视频事件推理的视觉语言模型（VLMs）需要高质量的结构化标注，不仅要捕捉发生了什么，还要捕捉何时、何地、为何以及产生了什么后果，而手动标注无法支持这种规模。我们提出了MAVEN（多阶段智能体视频事件标注），这是一个多阶段智能体流程，它将原始视频转化为带有思维链（CoT）推理轨迹的多任务训练数据，并围绕一个指定的焦点事件进行组织。MAVEN的核心是从三个互补的字幕级别合成一个多尺度时空事件描述（MSTED）；这个明确的中间表示作为下游多任务格式问答生成的唯一输入。至关重要的是，MAVEN支持智能体驱动的领域适应：给定一个新的视频数据集和目标问题示例，智能体无需手动重新设计，即可从上到下重新设计所有提示。一个分层优化循环进一步根据分类法对标注错误进行分类，将根本原因追溯到原始流程阶段，并应用有针对性的编辑来重写提示或修改流程结构本身，从而迭代地提高数据质量。我们将MAVEN应用于标注超过5,300个交通视频，并使用生成的数据微调了Cosmos-Reason2-8B。在私有CCTV评估集上，微调后的模型超越了Gemini 2.5 Pro和3.1 Flash，其中包括MCQ准确率比零样本提高了+38.8点。在AccidentBench上，仅CCTV训练使Cosmos-Reason2的MCQ得分提高了+10.7点，并与Gemini 2.5 Pro持平，尽管没有看到行车记录仪视频；添加智能体适应的行车记录仪标注缩小了与Gemini 3.1 Flash的差距，并且RL后训练将总体性能推向了超越两个Gemini基线。在仓库监控和公共安全视频上的定性结果进一步表明，智能体工作流可以很容易地将流程适应到新领域。
AI.summary: MAVEN是一个用于视频推理任务的多阶段智能体标注流程。它通过将原始视频转化为包含思维链推理轨迹的多任务训练数据，解决了VLM训练中高质量、大规模视频事件标注的挑战。MAVEN的核心是生成多尺度时空事件描述（MSTED），并支持智能体驱动的领域适应和分层错误修正，从而无需人工干预即可优化标注质量和适应新领域。实验表明，MAVEN生成的数据显著提升了Cosmos-Reason2-8B在交通视频和AccidentBench上的性能，超越了Gemini 2.5 Pro和3.1 Flash等基线模型，并展现了其在新领域的强大适应性。
AI.keywords: 视频推理,智能体标注,视觉语言模型,数据生成,领域适应
AI.comments: MAVEN的创新之处在于其多阶段智能体驱动的标注流程，特别是在大规模视频事件推理数据生成方面的自动化和自适应能力。它通过引入多尺度时空事件描述（MSTED）作为中间表示，简化了下游多任务生成。更重要的是，其智能体驱动的领域适应和分层错误修正循环，使得系统能够自我优化并适应新的数据和任务，大大减少了人工干预。这对于解决VLM训练中高质量、大规模、多领域视频标注的瓶颈具有重要意义。

title: Coupling-Robust Accuracy in Multiphysics Physics Informed Neural Networks via Kronecker-Preconditioned Optimization
comments: Extended version of AI4Physics Workshop accepted paper (ICML 2026)
summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for coupled multiphysics systems suffer systematic accuracy degradation as inter-equation coupling strengthens. We provide a theoretical explanation through neural tangent kernel (NTK) analysis: for linearly coupled systems, the standard NTK's spectral radius grows as $Ω(γ^2)$ with coupling strength $γ$, shrinking the stable learning rate, while block-diagonal Gauss--Newton (GN) preconditioning yields a preconditioned NTK $K_P = JH^{+}J^\top$ whose spectral radius is bounded by $S$ (number of networks), independent of $γ$. Adam's diagonal preconditioning destroys this projector structure -- inflating $λ_{\max}$ far above $S$ for any coupling type -- and its residual-dynamics kernel grows as $Θ(γ)$, placing its stable learning rate strictly between gradient descent and GN. For one-way coupling the limitation is class-wide: no diagonal preconditioner, fixed or adaptive, halves the driving residual in fewer than $Ω(γ)$ iterations ($Ω(γ^2)$ if fixed), whereas block-diagonal GN requires $O(1)$. We verify $Ω(γ^2)$ growth across linearly coupled benchmarks and confirm $λ_{\max}(K_P) = S$ in all three 1D systems, including nonlinearly coupled NP+P. Combining the Kronecker-preconditioned optimizer SOAP with inverse-gradient-norm loss balancing (SOAP+GradNorm) yields coupling-robust accuracy: across 222 experiments spanning three 1D systems and a 2D electroosmotic flow benchmark, SOAP+GradNorm maintains final-epoch $L_2$ accuracy across coupling strengths, with $\leq 2.3\times$ degradation in nonlinear NP+P while Adam+GradNorm fails ($L_2 > 0.1$). SOAP+GradNorm further scales to a 2D, 6-PDE electroosmotic flow at EDL-resolved conditions down to $\varepsilon = 0.01$ -- a regime all prior PINN electrokinetics studies have avoided -- where Adam+GradNorm fails entirely ($L_2 > 0.3$).
comment: Extended version of AI4Physics Workshop accepted paper (ICML 2026)

AI.title_translation: 耦合多物理场物理信息神经网络中通过克罗内克预条件优化实现耦合鲁棒精度
AI.tldr: 针对耦合多物理场物理信息神经网络中精度随耦合强度下降的问题，本文通过NTK分析揭示其根源，并提出克罗内克预条件优化（SOAP）结合梯度范数平衡（GradNorm）的方法，实现了在强耦合系统中的鲁棒精度和优越性能。
AI.motivation: 耦合多物理场物理信息神经网络（PINNs）在方程间耦合增强时会遭受系统性的精度下降。
AI.method: 1. 通过神经网络切线核（NTK）分析对精度下降问题提供理论解释，发现标准NTK的谱半径随耦合强度 $γ$ 呈 $Ω(γ^2)$ 增长。2. 提出块对角高斯-牛顿（GN）预条件处理，其预条件NTK的谱半径被网络数量 $S$ 限制，与 $γ$ 无关。3. 结合克罗内克预条件优化器SOAP与逆梯度范数损失平衡（GradNorm），形成SOAP+GradNorm方法。
AI.result: 1. 理论分析表明，标准NTK的谱半径随耦合强度 $γ$ 呈 $Ω(γ^2)$ 增长，导致稳定学习率缩小。2. 块对角GN预条件处理的NTK谱半径 $λ_{\max}(K_P)$ 被 $S$ 限制，与 $γ$ 无关。3. Adam的对角预条件处理破坏了这种投影结构，使 $λ_{\max}$ 远超 $S$。4. 对于单向耦合，任何对角预条件器都无法在少于 $Ω(γ)$ 次迭代中将驱动残差减半，而块对角GN只需 $O(1)$。5. 实验验证了1D线性耦合基准中 $Ω(γ^2)$ 增长，并在三种1D系统（包括非线性耦合NP+P）中确认 $λ_{\max}(K_P) = S$。6. SOAP+GradNorm在222个实验中（涵盖三种1D系统和2D电渗流基准）保持了跨耦合强度的最终 epoch $L_2$ 精度，在非线性NP+P中退化 $\leq 2.3$ 倍，而Adam+GradNorm失败。7. SOAP+GradNorm进一步扩展到2D、6-PDE电渗流的EDL解析条件（$\varepsilon = 0.01$），这是所有先前PINN电动力学研究都避免的区域，而Adam+GradNorm完全失败。
AI.conclusion: 结合克罗内克预条件优化器SOAP和逆梯度范数损失平衡（SOAP+GradNorm）的方法，在耦合多物理场PINNs中实现了耦合鲁棒的精度，并在强耦合和复杂2D电渗流等挑战性条件下显著优于现有方法。
AI.translation: 耦合多物理场物理信息神经网络（PINNs）在方程间耦合增强时会遭受系统性的精度下降。我们通过神经网络切线核（NTK）分析提供了一个理论解释：对于线性耦合系统，标准NTK的谱半径随耦合强度 $γ$ 呈 $Ω(γ^2)$ 增长，从而缩小了稳定的学习率；而块对角高斯-牛顿（GN）预条件处理产生的预条件NTK $K_P = JH^{+}J^\top$ 的谱半径被 $S$（网络数量）限制，与 $γ$ 无关。Adam的对角预条件处理破坏了这种投影结构——对于任何耦合类型，都会使 $λ_{\max}$ 远超 $S$——其残差动力学核呈 $Θ(γ)$ 增长，使其稳定学习率严格介于梯度下降和GN之间。对于单向耦合，这种限制是普遍存在的：无论是固定还是自适应的对角预条件器，都无法在少于 $Ω(γ)$ 次迭代中将驱动残差减半（如果固定，则为 $Ω(γ^2)$），而块对角GN只需 $O(1)$。我们在线性耦合基准中验证了 $Ω(γ^2)$ 的增长，并在所有三种1D系统（包括非线性耦合NP+P）中确认了 $λ_{\max}(K_P) = S$。结合克罗内克预条件优化器SOAP与逆梯度范数损失平衡（SOAP+GradNorm）实现了耦合鲁棒的精度：在涵盖三种1D系统和2D电渗流基准的222个实验中，SOAP+GradNorm在不同耦合强度下保持了最终 epoch 的 $L_2$ 精度，在非线性NP+P中退化 $\leq 2.3$ 倍，而Adam+GradNorm失败（$L_2 > 0.1$）。SOAP+GradNorm进一步扩展到2D、6-PDE电渗流的EDL解析条件，直至 $\varepsilon = 0.01$——这是所有先前PINN电动力学研究都避免的区域——而Adam+GradNorm完全失败（$L_2 > 0.3$）。
AI.summary: 本文研究了耦合多物理场物理信息神经网络（PINNs）在强耦合下精度下降的问题。通过神经网络切线核（NTK）分析，作者们揭示了标准优化器（如Adam）在处理强耦合系统时，其稳定学习率会因NTK谱半径的急剧增长而受限。为解决此问题，论文提出了一种基于克罗内克预条件优化器SOAP结合逆梯度范数损失平衡（SOAP+GradNorm）的方法。实验结果表明，SOAP+GradNorm在各种耦合强度下均能保持鲁棒的 $L_2$ 精度，并在复杂的非线性耦合系统及以前PINN无法处理的2D电渗流极端条件下，显著优于传统的Adam优化器，展现了其在多物理场PINNs应用中的优越性和潜力。
AI.keywords: 物理信息神经网络, 多物理场耦合, 克罗内克预条件优化, 神经网络切线核, 耦合鲁棒精度
AI.comments: 这篇论文的创新点在于通过严谨的神经网络切线核（NTK）理论分析，首次揭示了耦合多物理场PINNs在强耦合下精度下降的内在机制，即标准优化器导致NTK谱半径随耦合强度急剧增长。在此理论基础上，提出并验证了结合克罗内克预条件优化与损失平衡的SOAP+GradNorm方法，有效地解决了这一难题。其重要性在于，该方法不仅在理论上提供了坚实的基础，而且在实验中展现了卓越的性能，成功地将PINNs应用于之前无法解决的强耦合和复杂多物理场问题，特别是电渗流的EDL解析条件，极大地拓宽了PINNs的应用范围和解决实际工程问题的能力。

title: Perceptually Lossless Tactile Texture Synthesis with Compact Spectral Envelope Models
summary: Modern audio-visual media rely on compact representations for efficient storage and transmission, whereas realistic digital touch still depends on high-resolution tactile recordings. Existing approaches for representing tactile signals constrain manipulation and limit the generation of new content. Here, we introduce two compact representations, spectral beta and spectral slope, that capture the temporal spectral structure of finger-surface friction signals while preserving perceptually relevant information. Spectral beta models spectral skewness using a two-parameter beta distribution, whereas spectral slope approximates the spectrum with an asymmetric bandpass filter defined by low- and high-pass orders. We evaluated these representations in a perceptual study with 14 participants using five virtual textures rendered on a friction-modulation display and compared them with physical textures and high-fidelity reproductions of recorded signals. Spectral beta achieved perceptual similarity ratings comparable to those of the original high-fidelity reproductions. Regression analysis further showed that matching spectral energy across nine critical frequency bands was the strongest predictor of perceived realism. Together, these findings suggest that tactile texture perception depends primarily on fundamental temporal spectral patterns and that modeling these patterns is sufficient for perceptually realistic rendering. These results establish an efficient and scalable framework for haptic compression, communication, and synthetic texture generation.

AI.title_translation: 基于紧凑频谱包络模型的感知无损触觉纹理合成
AI.tldr: 该论文引入了两种紧凑的触觉纹理合成模型（频谱β和频谱斜率），实现了与高保真记录相似的感知无损结果，表明基本的时域频谱模式是触觉真实感的关键。
AI.motivation: 现代视听媒体依赖于紧凑的表示形式进行高效存储和传输，而逼真的数字触觉仍然依赖于高分辨率的触觉记录。现有的触觉信号表示方法限制了操作和新内容的生成。因此，本文旨在开发紧凑的触觉信号表示方法。
AI.method: 作者引入了两种紧凑表示：频谱β（使用双参数β分布模拟频谱偏度）和频谱斜率（通过不对称带通滤波器近似频谱）。他们通过一项包含14名参与者的感知研究评估了这些表示，使用摩擦调制显示器渲染了五种虚拟纹理，并与物理纹理和记录信号的高保真再现进行了比较。还使用了回归分析来预测感知真实感。
AI.result: 频谱β模型获得了与原始高保真再现相当的感知相似度评分。回归分析进一步表明，匹配九个关键频带的频谱能量是感知真实感的最强预测因子。
AI.conclusion: 触觉纹理感知主要取决于基本的时域频谱模式，建模这些模式足以实现感知上逼真的渲染。这些结果为触觉压缩、通信和合成纹理生成建立了一个高效且可扩展的框架。
AI.translation: 现代视听媒体依赖紧凑表示以实现高效存储和传输，而逼真的数字触觉仍然依赖高分辨率触觉记录。现有表示触觉信号的方法限制了操作并限制了新内容的生成。在此，我们引入了两种紧凑表示：频谱β和频谱斜率，它们捕捉指尖-表面摩擦信号的时域频谱结构，同时保留了感知相关信息。频谱β使用双参数β分布模拟频谱偏度，而频谱斜率通过由低通和高通阶数定义的非对称带通滤波器近似频谱。我们在一个包含14名参与者的感知研究中评估了这些表示，使用摩擦调制显示器渲染了五种虚拟纹理，并将其与物理纹理和记录信号的高保真再现进行了比较。频谱β实现了与原始高保真再现相当的感知相似度评分。回归分析进一步表明，匹配九个关键频带的频谱能量是感知真实感的最强预测因子。总而言之，这些发现表明触觉纹理感知主要取决于基本的时域频谱模式，并且建模这些模式足以实现感知上逼真的渲染。这些结果为触觉压缩、通信和合成纹理生成建立了一个高效且可扩展的框架。
AI.summary: 本论文提出了两种紧凑的频谱包络模型——频谱β和频谱斜率，用于合成感知无损的触觉纹理。与依赖高分辨率记录的传统方法不同，这些模型有效地捕捉了指尖-表面摩擦信号的时域频谱结构。一项感知研究表明，频谱β模型在感知相似度方面与高保真再现相当。研究结果强调了基本的时域频谱模式对于触觉真实感的重要性，并为触觉压缩、通信和合成纹理生成提供了一个高效且可扩展的框架。
AI.keywords: 触觉纹理合成, 频谱包络模型, 感知真实感, 触觉压缩, 频谱β
AI.comments: 这篇论文具有创新性，因为它摆脱了对高分辨率触觉记录的依赖，转而采用紧凑的、以感知为驱动的模型进行触觉纹理合成，类似于视听媒体的压缩方式。频谱β和频谱斜率模型的引入及其通过感知研究的验证，是迈向高效触觉渲染和通信的重要一步。其重要性在于能够实现可扩展的数字触觉体验。

title: Correcting Visual Blur Induced by Attention Distraction to Reduce Hallucinations: Algorithm and Theory
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) frequently suffer from object hallucinations, yet the visual perceptual mechanism underlying this failure remains poorly understood. In this work, we reveal that hallucinations are strongly associated with a human-like attention distraction phenomenon, where humans under divided focus experience degraded visual clarity and produce inaccurate descriptions, while in models the same mechanism manifests as spatial inconsistency in multi-head attention and temporal fading of attention to image tokens during decoding. We further provide theoretical insights that attention dispersion increases model complexity and degrades classification generalization. Motivated by these findings, we propose an Attention-Focused Approach for Improved Image Perception (AFIP), which corrects attention distraction via cross-head attention enrichment and reinforces visual grounding through dynamic historical attention enhancement. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks and models validate the effectiveness of AFIP without additional training. Code is available at: https://github.com/MIKUZ12/AFIP.

AI.title_translation: 纠正注意力分散引起的视觉模糊以减少幻觉：算法与理论
AI.tldr: 本文揭示了多模态大语言模型中的幻觉与注意力分散有关，并提出AFIP方法通过注意力增强来纠正视觉模糊，有效减少幻觉。
AI.motivation: 多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）常出现物体幻觉，但其背后的视觉感知机制尚不明确。本文旨在揭示幻觉与注意力分散的关联，并解决由此导致的视觉模糊问题，因为注意力分散会增加模型复杂性并降低分类泛化能力。
AI.method: 提出了一种名为AFIP（Attention-Focused Approach for Improved Image Perception）的注意力聚焦方法。该方法通过跨头注意力丰富化来纠正注意力分散，并通过动态历史注意力增强来强化视觉基础。
AI.result: 在多个基准和模型上的广泛实验验证了AFIP的有效性，且无需额外训练。
AI.conclusion: 本文揭示了MLLMs中幻觉与人类注意力分散现象的关联，并提供了理论见解。提出的AFIP方法通过纠正注意力分散和强化视觉基础，有效减少了幻觉，提升了模型的图像感知能力。
AI.translation: 多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）经常遭受物体幻觉的困扰，但导致这种失败的视觉感知机制仍知之甚少。在这项工作中，我们揭示幻觉与一种类似人类的注意力分散现象密切相关，在这种现象中，人类在注意力分散时会经历视觉清晰度下降并产生不准确的描述，而在模型中，相同的机制表现为多头注意力中的空间不一致性以及解码过程中对图像token注意力的时间衰减。我们进一步提供了理论见解，即注意力分散会增加模型复杂性并降低分类泛化能力。受这些发现的启发，我们提出了一种用于改进图像感知的注意力聚焦方法（AFIP），它通过跨头注意力丰富化来纠正注意力分散，并通过动态历史注意力增强来强化视觉基础。在多个基准和模型上进行的广泛实验验证了AFIP的有效性，且无需额外训练。代码可在：https://github.com/MIKUZ12/AFIP 获取。
AI.summary: 本文研究了多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）中物体幻觉的成因，发现其与类似人类的注意力分散现象紧密相关，表现为模型多头注意力中的空间不一致和解码时对图像token注意力的时间衰减。理论分析表明注意力分散会增加模型复杂性并损害分类泛化能力。为此，作者提出了一种注意力聚焦方法（AFIP），通过跨头注意力丰富化和动态历史注意力增强来纠正注意力分散，从而强化视觉基础。实验证明，AFIP无需额外训练即可有效减少幻觉。
AI.keywords: 多模态大语言模型, 物体幻觉, 注意力分散, 视觉感知, AFIP
AI.comments: 这篇论文通过将MLLMs的幻觉问题与人类注意力分散现象联系起来，提供了一个新颖的视角。其理论分析和提出的AFIP方法，特别是无需额外训练的特点，具有重要的实用价值和创新性，有望为解决多模态模型中的幻觉问题提供新的思路。

title: TrajAudit: Automated Failure Diagnosis for Agentic Coding Systems
summary:
Agentic systems have been widely studied to automate coding tasks such as bug fixing and feature implementation. As these systems increasingly operate on complex codebases, understanding where and why they fail becomes essential for iterative refinement and operational reliability. Existing automated failure diagnosis approaches leverage \textit{task execution trajectories}, yet they struggle with trajectories produced by repository-level coding agents due to two key properties. First, these trajectories are often long, spanning many execution steps, making it difficult for LLMs to track the causal chain of failure over the execution history. Second, these trajectories are laden with noise, containing substantial low-signal observations such as redundant program structures and verbose code context, which can interfere with LLM reasoning.
  To address these challenges, we propose \textit{TrajAudit}, an automated failure diagnosis framework specifically for trajectories produced by repository-level coding agents. TrajAudit employs an investigator agent supported by two modules: one reduces failure-irrelevant noisy context through semantic saliency folding, and the other derives preliminary diagnostic guidance from test failure reports as prior knowledge to help LLMs focus on likely failure regions. The investigator agent can further invoke tools to inspect folded content on demand, enabling a focused investigation without losing access to the full trajectory context. We also introduce \textit{RootSE}, a benchmark of 102 real-world instances from repository-level coding tasks, each annotated with the earliest decisive error step and a justification. Experiments on RootSE show that TrajAudit outperforms the strongest baselines by 10.8\% and 21.6\% in exact failure localization accuracy in the with- and without-reference settings, respectively, demonstrating its effectiveness.

AI.title_translation: TrajAudit：代理编码系统的自动化故障诊断
AI.tldr: TrajAudit是一个专门用于解决存储库级别编码代理生成轨迹的自动化故障诊断框架，通过减少噪声和提供诊断指导来提高故障定位准确性。
AI.motivation: 代理系统在自动化编码任务中广泛应用，但随着系统在复杂代码库上运行，理解其失败的原因和位置对于迭代改进和操作可靠性至关重要。现有方法在处理存储库级别编码代理生成的长且充满噪声的轨迹时存在困难，导致LLM难以跟踪故障因果链并受到低信号观测的干扰。
AI.method: 我们提出了TrajAudit，一个自动化故障诊断框架，专门用于处理存储库级别编码代理生成的轨迹。TrajAudit包含一个调查代理和两个支持模块：一个通过语义显著性折叠减少与故障无关的噪声上下文，另一个从测试失败报告中获取初步诊断指导作为先验知识，帮助LLM关注可能的故障区域。调查代理还可以按需调用工具检查折叠内容，实现有重点的调查同时不丢失完整的轨迹上下文。我们还引入了RootSE，一个包含102个真实世界实例的基准。
AI.result: 在RootSE基准测试中，TrajAudit在有参考和无参考设置下，其精确故障定位准确性分别比最强基线高出10.8%和21.6%。
AI.conclusion: TrajAudit通过解决长轨迹和噪声轨迹的挑战，显著提高了代理编码系统在存储库级别任务中的自动化故障诊断能力和准确性。
AI.translation:
代理系统已被广泛研究，以自动化诸如错误修复和功能实现等编码任务。随着这些系统越来越多地在复杂代码库上运行，了解它们在哪里以及为什么失败对于迭代改进和操作可靠性变得至关重要。现有的自动化故障诊断方法利用任务执行轨迹，但它们在处理由存储库级别编码代理生成的轨迹时遇到了困难，原因在于其两个关键特性。首先，这些轨迹通常很长，跨越许多执行步骤，使得大型语言模型（LLM）难以在执行历史中跟踪故障的因果链。其次，这些轨迹充满了噪声，包含大量低信号观测，例如冗余程序结构和冗长的代码上下文，这可能会干扰LLM的推理。
为了解决这些挑战，我们提出了TrajAudit，一个专门用于处理存储库级别编码代理生成的轨迹的自动化故障诊断框架。TrajAudit采用一个由两个模块支持的调查代理：一个通过语义显著性折叠减少与故障无关的噪声上下文，另一个从测试失败报告中获取初步诊断指导作为先验知识，以帮助LLM关注可能的故障区域。调查代理可以进一步按需调用工具检查折叠内容，从而在不丢失完整轨迹上下文的情况下实现有重点的调查。我们还引入了RootSE，一个包含102个来自存储库级别编码任务的真实世界实例的基准，每个实例都标注了最早的决定性错误步骤和理由。在RootSE上的实验表明，TrajAudit在有参考和无参考设置下，其精确故障定位准确性分别比最强基线高出10.8%和21.6%，证明了其有效性。
AI.summary: 本文提出了TrajAudit，一个针对存储库级别编码代理自动化故障诊断的框架。它解决了现有方法在处理长且噪声轨迹时的挑战，通过语义显著性折叠减少无关上下文，并利用测试失败报告提供诊断指导。TrajAudit引入了一个调查代理，可以按需检查折叠内容。通过在RootSE基准上的实验，TrajAudit在故障定位准确性方面显著优于现有基线。
AI.keywords: 故障诊断, 代理系统, 编码任务, LLM, TrajAudit
AI.comments: TrajAudit的创新之处在于其针对存储库级别编码代理轨迹的特殊性（长且噪声）提出了专门的解决方案。通过结合噪声上下文减少和先验知识指导，它有效地提升了LLM在复杂编码任务中故障诊断的准确性。RootSE基准的引入也为该领域的研究提供了有价值的评估工具。

title: A Dynamic Deontic Simplicial Logic for Joint Commitments
summary: We introduce the Deontic Simplicial Logic (DSL), a deontic logic for group obligations grounded in simplicial complexes: vertices encode individual commitments, and higher-dimensional simplices encode the joint commitments of the groups they connect. The resulting group modality behaves like a distributed-commitment operator with a genuinely normative character: it validates achievement but not the unrestricted introspection or monotonicity familiar from its epistemic counterpart, and impurity lets the model distinguish an agent's mere absence from a configuration from an explicit commitment to the contrary. We give a sound and complete axiomatization for the group modality. We then extend DSL to the Dynamic Deontic Simplicial Logic (DDSL), which introduces action modalities modeling agents' choices among mutually exclusive commitments, with effects captured by a product update construction on simplicial models; to our knowledge, this is the first dynamic deontic logic built on simplicial complexes. Soundness and completeness for DDSL are established via reduction axioms to the static case. Throughout, we illustrate both logics with worked examples of static and dynamic multi-agent commitment scenarios.

AI.title_translation: 联合承诺的动态道义单纯形逻辑
AI.tldr: 引入道义单纯形逻辑(DSL)及其动态扩展(DDSL)，用单纯形复形建模个体和联合承诺，并提供公理化和动态更新机制。
AI.motivation: 现有逻辑可能无法充分捕捉群体义务的复杂性，特别是区分单纯的缺席与明确的反对承诺，以及对代理人选择的动态建模。
AI.method: 1. 引入道义单纯形逻辑 (DSL)，将单纯形复形作为基础，其中顶点表示个体承诺，高维单纯形表示群体联合承诺。2. 描述群组模态作为具有规范特征的分布式承诺算子。3. 提供群组模态的完备性和可靠性公理化。4. 将DSL扩展为动态道义单纯形逻辑 (DDSL)，引入动作模态来建模代理人在互斥承诺间的选择，并使用乘积更新构造来捕捉效果。5. 通过归约公理建立DDSL的完备性和可靠性。
AI.result: 1. 提出了道义单纯形逻辑（DSL），其群组模态表现为具有规范特征的分布式承诺算子，能够验证成就，但不具有其认知对应物中常见的无限制内省或单调性。2. DSL模型能够区分代理人仅仅缺席于某种配置与明确地做出相反承诺。3. 为群组模态提供了可靠且完备的公理化。4. 提出了动态道义单纯形逻辑（DDSL），通过乘积更新构造建模代理人的选择和承诺效果，是首个基于单纯形复形的动态道义逻辑。5. 通过归约公理建立了DDSL的可靠性和完备性。
AI.conclusion: 本文成功引入了道义单纯形逻辑（DSL）及其动态扩展（DDSL），为建模个体和联合承诺提供了新颖且强大的形式化工具，特别是在处理群体义务的规范特性和动态演变方面，填补了现有研究的空白。
AI.translation: 我们引入了道义单纯形逻辑（DSL），这是一种基于单纯形复形的群体义务道义逻辑：顶点编码个体承诺，高维单纯形编码它们所连接群体的联合承诺。由此产生的群组模态行为类似于一个具有真正规范特征的分布式承诺算子：它验证成就，但不验证其认知对应物中常见的无限制内省或单调性，并且其“不纯性”允许模型区分代理人仅仅缺席于某种配置与明确地做出相反承诺。我们为群组模态提供了可靠且完备的公理化。然后，我们将DSL扩展为动态道义单纯形逻辑（DDSL），它引入了动作模态来建模代理人在互斥承诺间的选择，其效果通过单纯形模型上的乘积更新构造来捕捉；据我们所知，这是第一个建立在单纯形复形上的动态道义逻辑。DDSL的可靠性和完备性通过归约公理建立到静态情况。在整个过程中，我们通过静态和动态多代理承诺场景的实例来说明这两种逻辑。
AI.summary: 本文提出道义单纯形逻辑（DSL），利用单纯形复形建模个体和群体联合承诺，并定义了具有规范特征的群组模态，其具有特定的验证属性和区分能力。研究为群组模态提供了完备的公理化。在此基础上，文章进一步引入动态道义单纯形逻辑（DDSL），通过动作模态和乘积更新构造来捕捉代理人的选择及其承诺的动态变化，并声称这是首个基于单纯形复形的动态道义逻辑，其完备性通过归约公理得到证明。
AI.keywords: 道义逻辑, 单纯形复形, 群体承诺, 动态逻辑, 多代理系统
AI.comments: 这篇论文通过将单纯形复形引入道义逻辑，为建模复杂的个体和联合承诺提供了一个新颖且强大的框架。其创新点在于：1. 使用拓扑结构（单纯形复形）来表示承诺的结构，特别是联合承诺，这比传统的基于可能世界语义的道义逻辑更具表现力。2. 引入了动态扩展DDSL，通过乘积更新机制处理承诺的动态演变和代理人的选择，填补了该领域的一个空白。3. 明确区分了代理人的缺席与明确的反对承诺，这在实际应用中具有重要意义。这一方法为理解和形式化多代理系统中的群体规范和动态交互提供了新的视角。

title: A Lumped-Element Electrical Model of the Human Head for Brain-Oriented Applications
comments: 4 pages, 4 figures. To appear in the proceedings of the APS March Meeting 2026, Detroit, Michigan
summary: In this work, we present a compact surrogate circuit for electro-quasi-static (EQS) head modeling. A three-shell geometry (brain, skull, scalp) is considered, and each layer is modeled through radial and tangential pathways, implemented as RC branches. Frequency-dependent tissue conductivity and permittivity are mapped into dispersive resistive and capacitive elements. The model is validated against a semi-analytical spherical-harmonics reference solution over multiple geometrical configurations and operating frequencies, demonstrating good agreement. Neglecting dispersion and capacitive pathways can lead to an overestimation of scalp potentials over the considered frequency range, highlighting the need for dispersive RC circuit modeling.
comment: 4 pages, 4 figures. To appear in the proceedings of the APS March Meeting 2026, Detroit, Michigan

AI.title_translation: 人头部的集总元件电学模型在脑部应用中的研究
AI.tldr: 提出了一个紧凑的集总元件电路模型，用于脑电准静态头部建模，考虑了频率相关的组织特性，并强调了色散RC电路建模的重要性。
AI.motivation: 现有模型可能忽视了色散和容性通路，导致头皮电位过高估计，因此需要一个更准确的、考虑频率相关特性的电学模型。
AI.method: 提出了一个紧凑的替代电路，用于电准静态(EQS)头部建模。该模型考虑了三层几何结构（脑、颅骨、头皮），每层通过径向和切向路径建模为RC支路。频率相关的组织电导率和介电常数被映射为色散电阻和电容元件。模型通过与半解析球谐参考解进行验证。
AI.result: 模型在多种几何配置和工作频率下与半解析球谐参考解表现出良好的一致性。忽略色散和容性通路会导致在所考虑的频率范围内头皮电位被高估。
AI.conclusion: 为了准确地模拟人头部的电学行为，特别是在脑部应用中，需要使用考虑频率相关色散和容性通路的RC电路模型。
AI.translation: 在这项工作中，我们提出了一个用于电准静态（EQS）头部建模的紧凑替代电路。模型考虑了三层几何结构（脑、颅骨、头皮），每一层都通过径向和切向路径进行建模，这些路径以RC支路的形式实现。频率依赖的组织电导率和介电常数被映射到色散电阻和电容元件中。该模型在多种几何配置和工作频率下，通过与半解析球谐参考解进行验证，并表现出良好的一致性。忽略色散和容性通路可能导致在所考虑的频率范围内头皮电位被高估，这凸显了色散RC电路建模的必要性。
AI.summary: 这项工作提出了一个用于电准静态头部建模的紧凑集总元件电路模型。该模型将人头部建模为三层结构（脑、颅骨、头皮），每层由径向和切向的RC支路表示，并考虑了频率相关的组织电导率和介电常数。模型通过与半解析参考解的验证，显示出良好的准确性，并强调了在脑部应用中，考虑色散和容性通路对于避免头皮电位过高估计的重要性。
AI.keywords: 人头模型, 集总元件, 电准静态, RC电路, 色散
AI.comments: 这项工作提出了一种有效且紧凑的头部电学模型，通过将频率相关的组织特性映射到色散RC元件中，提高了建模的准确性。其创新点在于强调了色散和容性通路在EQS头部建模中的关键作用，对于脑电图（EEG）等脑部应用具有重要意义。

title: ZAPS-DA: Zero-Phase Action Policy Smoothing with Decoupled Actor for Continuous Control in Reinforcement Learning
comments: 9 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles
summary: Continuous control policies trained with off-policy reinforcement learning frequently exhibit high-frequency action jitter, impractical for direct deployment on physical actuators. Post-hoc filtering attenuates jitter but adds phase lag; embedding smoothness penalties in the actor's loss couples them with the RL gradient and conflates reward regression with over-aggressive smoothing. We present ZAPS-DA, which reduces action jitter at deployment with negligible phase lag and no post-processing. ZAPS-DA pairs an unmodified main actor (trained by the base RL loss) with a separate decoupled actor trained via supervised imitation of zero-phase filtered targets stored in the replay buffer. The deployed policy is the decoupled actor: a feed-forward map from observation to smooth action, with no inference-time filter and no action-history input -- causal distillation of a non-causal filter. A magnitude-matched MSE loss gives zero-hyperparameter portability across optimizer classes. Validated with Soft Actor-Critic and a Savitzky-Golay filter in two driving simulators (paired n=150): on MetaDrive (anchor protocol), ZAPS-DA cuts steering jitter 14-21x and throttle jitter 3-5x (all $p<10^{-4}$, Bonferroni) while matching task-completion (p=0.28 success, p=0.31 crash) at 6.3% reward cost; on a custom Webots adaptive cruise control task, the same configuration yields a Pareto improvement -- reward parity (p=0.121), 8-45x steering-jitter reduction, task-failure rate 2.0% to 0.7%. Against CAPS, the standard penalty-based baseline -- at both its auto-entropy and native fixed-entropy operating points, with penalty weight, spatial noise, and entropy coefficient re-tuned per environment -- ZAPS-DA reaches 14.7x steering-jitter reduction versus CAPS's best 3.2x at matched seeds, a ~4.6x gap, with no per-environment tuning of the smoothness signal and post-hoc applicability to trained policies.
comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles

AI.title_translation: ZAPS-DA：基于解耦Actor的零相位动作策略平滑用于强化学习中的连续控制
AI.tldr: ZAPS-DA通过一个解耦的Actor，利用零相位过滤目标进行监督模仿学习，在不增加相位滞后的情况下显著减少了强化学习连续控制中的动作抖动。
AI.motivation: 离策略强化学习训练的连续控制策略常表现出高频动作抖动，不适合直接部署在物理执行器上。现有方法（如事后滤波）会增加相位滞后，而将平滑惩罚嵌入到Actor的损失中则会将奖励回归与过度平滑混淆。
AI.method: ZAPS-DA将一个未修改的主Actor（由基础RL损失训练）与一个单独的解耦Actor配对。解耦Actor通过对存储在回放缓冲区中的零相位过滤目标进行监督模仿学习来训练。部署的策略是这个解耦Actor，它是一个从观察到平滑动作的前馈映射，没有推理时滤波器和动作历史输入。使用幅度匹配的MSE损失，实现了零超参数的优化器类别可移植性。
AI.result: 在MetaDrive（n=150）上，ZAPS-DA将转向抖动减少了14-21倍，油门抖动减少了3-5倍（所有p<10^-4），同时保持了任务完成率（成功p=0.28，碰撞p=0.31），奖励成本为6.3%。在Webots自适应巡航控制任务中，实现了帕累托改进：奖励持平（p=0.121），转向抖动减少8-45倍，任务失败率从2.0%降至0.7%。与CAPS相比，ZAPS-DA实现了14.7倍的转向抖动减少，而CAPS的最佳表现为3.2倍，差距约为4.6倍，且ZAPS-DA无需对平滑信号进行每环境调优。
AI.conclusion: ZAPS-DA在连续控制强化学习中有效减少了动作抖动，同时避免了相位滞后和事后处理的需要，并在性能上优于现有基线。
AI.translation: 离策略强化学习训练的连续控制策略经常表现出高频动作抖动，这对于在物理执行器上直接部署是不切实际的。事后滤波可以衰减抖动，但会增加相位滞后；将平滑惩罚嵌入到Actor的损失中会使其与RL梯度耦合，并将奖励回归与过度激进的平滑混淆。我们提出了ZAPS-DA，它在部署时减少了动作抖动，相位滞后可忽略不计，且无需事后处理。ZAPS-DA将一个未修改的主Actor（由基础RL损失训练）与一个单独的解耦Actor配对，该解耦Actor通过对存储在回放缓冲区中的零相位过滤目标进行监督模仿学习来训练。部署的策略是这个解耦Actor：一个从观察到平滑动作的前馈映射，没有推理时滤波器和动作历史输入——非因果滤波器的一种因果蒸馏。幅度匹配的MSE损失为优化器类别提供了零超参数可移植性。在两个驾驶模拟器中（配对n=150），使用软Actor-Critic和Savitzky-Golay滤波器进行了验证：在MetaDrive（锚定协议）上，ZAPS-DA将转向抖动减少了14-21倍，油门抖动减少了3-5倍（所有p<10^-4，Bonferroni校正），同时保持了任务完成率（成功p=0.28，碰撞p=0.31），奖励成本为6.3%；在定制的Webots自适应巡航控制任务中，相同的配置产生了帕累托改进——奖励持平（p=0.121），转向抖动减少8-45倍，任务失败率从2.0%降至0.7%。与标准基于惩罚的基线CAPS相比——在其自动熵和原生固定熵操作点上，并根据每个环境重新调整惩罚权重、空间噪声和熵系数——ZAPS-DA在匹配的随机种子下达到了14.7倍的转向抖动减少，而CAPS的最佳表现为3.2倍，差距约为4.6倍，且ZAPS-DA无需对平滑信号进行每环境调优，并可事后应用于已训练的策略。
AI.summary: 该论文提出了ZAPS-DA，一种用于连续控制强化学习的新方法，旨在解决离策略RL中常见的动作抖动问题。ZAPS-DA通过将一个标准RL训练的主Actor与一个单独的解耦Actor相结合来实现这一点，解耦Actor通过模仿零相位过滤的动作目标进行监督学习。这种方法在部署时提供了平滑的动作，且无需额外的相位滞后或事后处理。实验结果表明，ZAPS-DA在减少动作抖动方面显著优于现有基线，同时保持或提高任务性能，并且无需复杂的超参数调优。
AI.keywords: 强化学习, 连续控制, 动作平滑, 解耦Actor, 零相位
AI.comments: ZAPS-DA的创新之处在于其解耦Actor的设计，它将动作平滑从主RL训练中分离出来，避免了传统平滑惩罚方法中奖励回归与过度平滑的混淆问题。通过模仿零相位过滤目标，它能够在不引入相位滞后的情况下实现显著的抖动抑制，这对于物理世界的部署至关重要。其零超参数可移植性也大大简化了应用。该方法能够事后应用于已训练的策略，增加了其灵活性和实用价值。

title: Benchmarking Recursive-Collapse Warning Claims Under Matched False-Positive Control
comments: 29 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables; supplementary materials: 9 pages, 1 figure, 4 tables. Code, derived data packets, and Lean artifact: https://github.com/davidmullett/loopzero-paper-public (release tag lean-v1.0)
summary:
Recursive systems can enter collapse-like regimes -- self-reinforcing amplification, persistent recursion, and narrowing diversity that mask accelerating internal degradation -- before overt failure becomes visible. We introduce Loopzero, a claim-bounded benchmark framework for testing whether recursive failures follow a directional telemetry pattern: rising gain (G), recursive persistence (p), and declining diversity ($δ$). The claim boundary is specified in Lean; the Lean artifact does not verify real telemetry, benchmark validity, or detector performance.
  We evaluate the bridge on two frozen public-artifact benchmarks: a segmented public-markets benchmark (Volmageddon 2018, COVID MWCB 2020) and a MovieLens-25M offline deterministic recommender replay. Detectors are evaluated under a locked equal-false-positive contract (FP $\in$ [0.03, 0.07], pre-registered) so all configurations face the same alert budget. Neither tested standard comparators nor Loopzero's pre-registered quantile detector achieved an accepted operating point. Directional witness alignment held on both canonical benchmarks, with adjacent-horizon and row-level limitations disclosed. Digitized Shumailov et al. (2024) LLM training-loop trajectories are directionally consistent with the pattern; matched-FP evaluation in that domain is deferred.
  The contribution is a reproducible, falsifiable benchmark framework for evaluating recursive-collapse warning claims under an explicit alert-budget contract -- non-acceptance reported as a first-class scientific outcome.
comment: 29 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables; supplementary materials: 9 pages, 1 figure, 4 tables. Code, derived data packets, and Lean artifact: https://github.com/davidmullett/loopzero-paper-public (release tag lean-v1.0)

AI.title_translation: 在匹配假阳性控制下对递归崩溃预警声明进行基准测试
AI.tldr: 本文介绍了Loopzero，一个在匹配假阳性控制下评估递归系统崩溃预警声明的基准测试框架。研究发现，尽管现有检测器未达预期，但递归故障的方向性模式在基准测试中得到验证。主要贡献是一个可复现、可证伪的基准测试框架，强调将未接受结果作为重要的科学发现。
AI.motivation: 递归系统在显式故障可见之前可能进入类似崩溃的状态，表现为自我强化放大、持续递归和多样性收窄。本研究的动机是测试递归故障是否遵循特定的方向性遥测模式：增益上升（G）、递归持久性（p）和多样性下降（$δ$）。
AI.method: 本文引入了Loopzero，一个声明有界的基准测试框架，用于测试递归故障是否遵循特定的方向性遥测模式。该框架在两个公开基准数据集上进行评估：公共市场基准（Volmageddon 2018, COVID MWCB 2020）和MovieLens-25M离线确定性推荐器回放。所有检测器都在锁定的等假阳性合同下（FP $\in$ [0.03, 0.07]）进行评估。
AI.result: 经过测试，标准比较器和Loopzero预注册的分位数检测器均未达到可接受的操作点。然而，在两个规范基准上，方向性证据对齐成立，但也披露了相邻视野和行级别限制。数字化后的Shumailov et al. (2024) LLM训练循环轨迹与该模式方向一致。
AI.conclusion: 本文的贡献是一个可复现、可证伪的基准测试框架，用于在明确的警报预算合同下评估递归崩溃预警声明，并将未接受结果报告为一流的科学成果。
AI.translation:
递归系统在显式故障变得可见之前，可能会进入类似崩溃的状态——自我强化的放大、持续的递归以及掩盖加速内部退化的多样性收窄。我们引入了Loopzero，一个声明有界的基准测试框架，用于测试递归故障是否遵循方向性遥测模式：增益上升（G）、递归持久性（p）和多样性下降（$δ$）。声明边界在Lean中指定；Lean工件不验证真实的遥测数据、基准有效性或检测器性能。
我们在两个冻结的公共工件基准上评估了该桥梁：一个分段的公共市场基准（2018年Volmageddon事件，2020年COVID MWCB）和一个MovieLens-25M离线确定性推荐器回放。检测器在锁定的等假阳性合同下（FP $\in$ [0.03, 0.07]，已预注册）进行评估，因此所有配置都面临相同的警报预算。测试的标准比较器和Loopzero预注册的分位数检测器均未达到可接受的操作点。方向性证据对齐在两个规范基准上均成立，并披露了相邻视野和行级别限制。数字化后的Shumailov et al. (2024) LLM训练循环轨迹与该模式方向一致；该领域的匹配假阳性评估被推迟。
本文的贡献是一个可复现、可证伪的基准测试框架，用于在明确的警报预算合同下评估递归崩溃预警声明——将未接受报告作为一流的科学成果。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了Loopzero，一个用于基准测试递归系统崩溃预警声明的框架。该框架旨在验证递归故障是否遵循增益上升、递归持久性和多样性下降的方向性遥测模式。通过在公共市场和推荐系统数据集上的评估，研究发现尽管现有检测器未能达到理想操作点，但方向性模式在基准测试中得到了验证。最终，本文提出了一个可复现、可证伪的基准测试框架，强调将未接受的结果视为重要的科学发现。
AI.keywords: 递归系统, 崩溃预警, 基准测试, 假阳性控制, Loopzero
AI.comments: 本文的创新之处在于提出了一个专门用于评估递归系统崩溃预警的基准测试框架Loopzero，并强调了在严格的假阳性控制下进行评估。其重要性在于提供了一个科学、可复现的方法来探测复杂系统中潜在的崩溃模式，并将“未接受”的实验结果视为有价值的科学成果，这有助于推动研究的透明度和可靠性。

title: SHARP: Sleep-based Hierarchical Accelerated Replay for Long Range Non-Stationary Temporal Pattern Recognition
summary: Learning long-range non-stationary temporal patterns remains a core challenge for modern sequence models, particularly in strict streaming settings. In these settings, data arrive sequentially and must be processed in a single pass without simultaneously revisiting past observations. Standard architectures, including recurrent neural networks and transformers, are constrained by either truncated backpropagation through time horizon or explicit input window length for long range credit assignment. To address these limitations, we propose SHARP (Sleep-based Hierarchical Accelerated Replay), a framework that decomposes temporal learning into two complementary components: a memory module that accumulates a structured history of past inputs, and a pattern-recognition module that operates over this memory. This separation enables resource- and compute-efficient adaptation to non-stationary dynamics by eliminating the need for backpropagation through time across many steps for long-range credit assignment. Inspired by the accelerated replay observed in rodents during slow-wave sleep, SHARP incorporates offline (sleep) phases in which temporally structured memory traces are replayed in an accelerated form and integrated into higher-level memory representations, improving long-range context retention. Through controlled simulations and ablation studies, we characterize the key properties of the proposed framework. In benchmark datasets such as text8 and PG-19, we demonstrate that SHARP improves over recurrent baselines by retaining next-token predictive performance on previously seen data while continuing to learn from the current stream and generalizing to future unseen data. These gains are enabled by its hierarchical structure, which yields an exponentially increasing effective temporal context with only linear-time computational cost.

AI.title_translation: SHARP：基于睡眠的分层加速重放用于长距离非平稳时间模式识别
AI.tldr: SHARP是一种受睡眠启发的框架，通过将时间学习分解为记忆和模式识别模块，并利用加速重放来解决流式设置中长距离非平稳时间模式识别的挑战，从而在长距离上下文保持和预测性能上超越了现有模型。
AI.motivation: 现代序列模型在严格的流式设置中，学习长距离非平稳时间模式仍然是一个核心挑战。现有的循环神经网络和Transformer等架构，由于截断反向传播时间范围或显式输入窗口长度的限制，难以进行长距离的信用分配。
AI.method: SHARP（基于睡眠的分层加速重放）框架将时间学习分解为两个互补的组件：一个记忆模块用于积累结构化的历史输入，和一个模式识别模块用于操作此记忆。这种分离通过消除在许多步骤中进行长距离信用分配的反向传播时间需求，实现了资源和计算效率高的非平稳动态适应。受啮齿动物慢波睡眠期间加速重放的启发，SHARP结合了离线（睡眠）阶段，在此阶段中，时间结构化的记忆痕迹以加速形式重放并整合到更高层次的记忆表示中，从而改善了长距离上下文保留。
AI.result: 通过受控模拟和消融研究，SHARP的特性得到了表征。在text8和PG-19等基准数据集上，SHARP在保留先前数据的下一个词预测性能的同时，继续从当前流中学习并泛化到未来未见数据，从而优于循环基线。这些提升得益于其分层结构，该结构以线性时间计算成本实现了指数级增长的有效时间上下文。
AI.conclusion: SHARP框架通过其独特的记忆和模式识别模块分离以及受睡眠启发的加速重放机制，有效地解决了在严格流式设置中学习长距离非平稳时间模式的挑战，显著提升了长距离上下文保留和预测性能，并具有高效的计算成本。

AI.summary: SHARP是一种受睡眠启发的框架，旨在解决严格流式设置中长距离非平稳时间模式识别的难题。它将时间学习分解为记忆和模式识别模块，通过在“睡眠”阶段加速重放历史记忆痕迹，来有效整合并改善长距离上下文保留，避免了传统模型在长距离信用分配上的限制。实验证明，SHARP在基准数据集上优于循环基线，在保持对已见数据的预测性能的同时，能持续学习新数据并泛化到未见数据，其分层结构以线性计算成本实现了指数级增长的有效时间上下文。
AI.keywords: 长距离时间模式, 非平稳数据, 序列模型, 记忆重放, 分层学习
AI.comments: SHARP的创新之处在于其将生物学上“睡眠”的概念引入到机器学习模型中，通过分层加速重放机制，巧妙地解决了传统序列模型在处理长距离非平稳时间模式和信用分配方面的固有局限性。这种受生物启发的设计，特别是记忆模块和模式识别模块的分离，以及离线重放策略，使其在资源和计算效率上具有优势。该方法对于需要处理连续数据流和适应动态变化的领域具有重要意义。

title: The World's Fastest Matching Engine Algorithm
summary: We benchmarked every common open-source FIFO matching-engine implementation we could find, deduplicated, and driven through a single C-ABI harness on one identical workload - 246 distinct engines across more than twenty programming languages. The workload doubles as a byte-identical correctness oracle, and it is unforgiving: only 47 are correct as shipped; it surfaced 267+ distinct defects across the other 199, and we filed 172+ GitHub issues upstream. Our engine leads the 160 that reproduce the consensus by +25 M/s (roughly 4x from the second best) on worst-case throughput, and outruns every engine in the survey written by a professional trading-industry engineer. A single CPU core sustains 33.2~million order messages per second at sub-microsecond median end-to-end host-path latency; a 96-core commodity server (~$1,630/month) sustains ~640 million messages per second across 10,000 symbols - over 20x the provisioned capacity of the U.S. consolidated quote feed.

title: From Performance to Viability: A Bootstrap Framework for Latent-Space Representation Learning in Adaptive Biological Systems
comments: 25 pages. Methodological framework for latent-space representation learning in adaptive biological systems
summary: Observable performance is commonly used to characterize biological systems. In adaptive systems, however, similar performances may arise from distinct organizations, and configurations that appear comparable at a given time may follow different longitudinal trajectories. This limitation motivates a methodological framework for moving beyond performance-based interpretation without assuming a complete mechanistic model in advance. This article proposes a bootstrap framework for latent-space representation learning in adaptive biological systems. Here, bootstrap is used in a methodological and epistemological sense: theory is not imposed a priori, but progressively emerges from the limitations encountered in observation. The framework is organized around five levels: observable performance, dynamic organization, latent organization, observed longitudinal viability, and internal predictive approximation. The framework is illustrated by three previously reported gait-occlusion studies, used here only as a methodological case sequence and not as new experimental evidence. The article formalizes how performance analysis led to latent organization, how static latent organization led to observed longitudinal viability, and how observed viability led to internal predictive approximation. The contribution is therefore not a new learning algorithm, clinical protocol, or dataset, but a bootstrap framework for latent-space representation learning describing how increasingly informative representations can emerge from observational insufficiencies in adaptive biological data.
comment: 25 pages. Methodological framework for latent-space representation learning in adaptive biological systems

title: When RLHF Fails: A Mechanistic Taxonomy of Reward Hacking, Collapse, and Evaluator Gaming
comments: 20 pages, 8 figures; includes code, artifacts, and live demo
summary: RLHF evaluation should track how failures emerge, where they localize, and which warning signals appear before external quality degrades. We study this problem with a compact RLHF pipeline built for this paper, including PPO, DPO, uncertainty-penalized PPO (UP-PPO), reward-model uncertainty, approximate policy drift, diversity and repetition diagnostics, and two external LLM judges. Rather than treating reward hacking as a single terminal event, we classify matched checkpoint and prompt-level transitions by the directions of learned reward R_phi, judge scores R_dag and R2_dag, and their average R_dag. The main empirical findings are that aggressive PPO produces the clearest localized reward-hacking signal, UP-PPO reduces but does not eliminate that signal, row-level diagnostics reveal failures hidden by checkpoint averages, and pre-transition features partially anticipate future localized reward hacking. The central conclusion is methodological: RLHF failures are training dynamics that can be classified, localized, and partially anticipated, not only final-model pathologies. The repository is available at github.com/zabahana/rlhf-failure-modes-diagnostics. The pipeline is also deployed as a live interactive web demo for model comparison and diagnostic views at rlhf-failures.zelalem.ai.
comment: 20 pages, 8 figures; includes code, artifacts, and live demo

title: Temporal Preference Concepts and their Functions in a Large Language Model
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being deployed to make decisions that require trading off near-term gains against long-term consequences, yet little is known about how they internally represent or resolve these tradeoffs. In this work, we causally localize an underlying subgraph for temporal preference in a distilled LLM (Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507), identifying mid-to-upper-layer nodes through converging evidence from gradient-based attribution and activation patching. We find that the geometry of time horizon is encoded in the residual stream at the expected localized layers. A behavioral analysis reveals that unintervened LLMs discount the future several times less steeply than humans, yet this preference is unstable across contexts, motivating explicit control rather than implicit reliance on training. Finally, we find suggestive evidence that steering vectors can shift temporal preference. Our work demonstrates how mechanistic interpretability can bring us closer to reliable control over how LLMs plan and reason

title: AdaPlanBench: Evaluating Adaptive Planning in Large Language Model Agents under World and User Constraints
summary: Planning for real-world problems by language models often involves both world and user constraints, which may not be fully specified upfront and are progressively disclosed through interaction. However, existing benchmarks still underexplore adaptive planning under such progressively revealed dual constraints. To address this gap, we introduce AdaPlanBench, a dynamic interactive benchmark for evaluating whether Large Language Model (LLM) agents can adaptively plan and re-plan under progressively revealed world and user constraints. AdaPlanBench is built on 307 household tasks, with a scalable constraint construction pipeline that augments each task with dual constraints. At runtime, agents interact with the environment in a multi-turn protocol where hidden constraints are revealed only when the agent proposes a plan that violates them, requiring iterative plan revision under accumulating feedback. This makes planning challenging, as agents must infer and track constraints from feedback while re-planning effectively. Experiments on ten leading LLMs show that adaptive planning under dual constraints remains challenging, with the best model reaching only 67.75% accuracy. We further observe that performance degrades as more constraints accumulate, with user constraints posing a particularly large challenge and failures often stemming from weaker physical grounding and reduced effectiveness. These results establish AdaPlanBench as a testbed for dual-constrained interactive planning and highlight the challenge of reliable adaptation to dynamically revealed constraints in LLM agents.

title: A Sliced-Wasserstein Framework on Correlation Matrices for EEG Decoding
summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) offers noninvasive, millisecond resolution recordings of neuronal activity and is widely used in neuroscience and healthcare. Many EEG decoding pipelines rely on covariance descriptors for their robustness to noise, but such representations are sensitive to channel-wise scaling. Recent studies have therefore advocated full-rank correlation matrices as a scale-invariant alternative for EEG decoding. In this paper, we study Sliced-Wasserstein (SW) discrepancies for probability distributions on the manifold of full-rank correlation matrices. We adopt the pullback-Euclidean formulation of SW, referred to as Pullback Euclidean Metric Sliced-Wasserstein (PEMSW), and instantiate it under two recently introduced correlation geometries, \textit{i.e.}, the Off-Log Metric (OLM) and Log-Scaled Metric (LSM). This yields two Correlation Sliced-Wasserstein (CorSW) discrepancies with closed-form slicing coordinates and efficient computation through one-dimensional Wasserstein distances. Building on CorSW, we further develop a domain generalization (DG) framework for EEG decoding. Experiments on three EEG datasets demonstrate improved generalization under distribution shifts, with low training overhead and no additional inference cost. The source code is available at github.com/ChenHu-ML/CorSW.

title: EasyLens: A Training-Free Plug-and-Play Subtle-Lesion Representation Amplifier for Medical Vision-Language Models
summary: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) have shown increasing potential for clinical image interpretation, including lesion detection and report generation. However, their practical utility remains limited by insufficient sensitivity to subtle lesions, whose visual evidence is often sparse, low-contrast, and embedded within complex anatomical context. As local visual tokens are aggregated, these weak lesion cues can become underrepresented in global image representations, making them difficult for medical VLMs to recognize. Existing efforts to improve lesion sensitivity mainly rely on medical-domain vision-encoder pre-training, clinical-term-guided alignment, or trainable pathological representation enhancement. Although effective, these approaches usually require additional training or model-specific adaptation and may overfit to particular disease morphologies, limiting their applicability to frozen medical VLMs. To address these limitations, we propose EasyLens, a training-free plug-and-play subtle-lesion representation amplifier for medical VLMs. EasyLens first constructs EasyBank, a pathology-anatomy prototype space that provides lesion-related prototypes and anatomy-aware normal references for comparing suspicious patches against both pathological and normal anatomical patterns. To avoid blindly amplifying normal tissues, EasyTag selects lesion-relevant patches through counterfactual prototype reasoning. To counteract the dilution of subtle lesion cues in global image representations, EasyAmplifier strengthens the selected lesion-relevant patch representations through morphology-guided residual enhancement, thereby increasing their contribution to the global image embedding. Experiments on multiple medical image datasets and frozen medical VLM backbones show that EasyLens improves subtle-lesion detection and outperforms existing encoder-enhancement baselines.

title: EFX for Additive Chores: Nonexistence, Pareto Incompatibility, and Bi-Valued Existence
summary:
We consider the fair division problem of indivisible chores and resolve the long-standing open problem for the existence of EFX (envy-free up to any item) allocations with additive cost functions. We show that, even for tri-valued additive cost functions, for every $n\geq 4$, there exists an instance with $n$ agents where no EFX allocation exists. Our counterexample only uses three types of chores and two types of agents. The numbers of types for chores and agents are both tight: an EFX allocation is known to exist for one type of agents (i.e., with identical cost functions) or two types of chores.
  We then consider bi-valued instances. We show that, for every $n\geq 4$, there exists an instance with $n$ agents where every EFX allocation is not Pareto-optimal. This is also the first example showing the incompatibility of EFX and Pareto-optimality when the costs of items are positive: existing examples showing the incompatibility of EFX and Pareto-optimal exploit items with $0$ costs. Our result shows such an example exists even for bi-valued instances. The number of agents $n$ is also tight: for $n\leq 3$, it is known that EFX is compatible with Pareto-optimality. Finally, we also show that an EFX allocation is guaranteed to exist for $n=4$.

title: Deployment-Time Memorization in Foundation-Model Agents
summary: Foundation-model agents are increasingly long-lived systems that remember users across interactions, making memorization an explicit deployment-time function rather than solely a property of model weights. Existing work addresses parametric memorization or audits fixed memory configurations, but does not characterize how memory-design choices jointly shape personalization utility, extraction risk, and deletion fidelity. We study this surface as deployment-time memorization, formulating agent memory as a privacy-utility frontier measured by Personalization Recall (PR) and Adversarial Extraction Rate (AER), and sweeping three memory-design knobs: summarization aggressiveness, retrieval breadth (k), and deletion mode. We further introduce the Forgetting Residue Score (FRS) to quantify whether deleted information remains recoverable from derived memory tiers. On LongMemEval, key-fact summarization reduces canary extraction by 76% on Gemma 3 12B and 64% on GPT-4o-mini while preserving nearly all personalization recall; critically, once content is compressed away, increasing k no longer restores leakage. The same compression, however, induces a deletion-fidelity failure: raw-only deletion leaves derived summary copies recoverable in approximately 20% of instances, and only full-pipeline purge or tombstone redaction drives worst-tier residue to zero. Together, these results establish that persistent agent memory must be evaluated as a first-class memorization mechanism -- assessed by what it helps agents recall, what it makes extractable, and what it can truly erase.

title: KG-SoftMAP: Soft Knowledge-Graph Priors for Bayesian Network Structure Learning from Sparse Discrete Data
comments: 12 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables; includes a 24-page technical supplement
summary: Learning Bayesian network (BN) structure from sparse discrete data is hard: when each instance records only a few variables, most variable pairs lack the joint observations needed for reliable scoring, and data-only methods recover little structure. Imperfect domain knowledge, expressible as a weighted directed knowledge graph (KG), is often available. KG-SoftMAP encodes such a KG as a finite-strength, confidence-weighted edge prior and maximizes a MAP objective that adds this logit-form prior to the BDeu score. With an informative but imperfect KG, KG-SoftMAP recovers partial directed structure even at observation rate rho=0.05, with directed F1 (DF1) of 0.19-0.32 across benchmarks. At higher observation rates within this sparse grid, DF1 reaches 0.44-0.66 at rho=0.20 and 0.46-0.64 at rho=0.40. Across the same three rates, KG-SoftMAP without the KG prior averages DF1 0.00, 0.19, and 0.21. Stress tests that corrupt, remove, or blur the KG signal, together with checks on LLM-extracted graphs beyond canonical benchmarks, show that recovery rises and falls with KG quality. On three real sparse educational datasets without ground-truth DAGs, we evaluate prediction, calibration, and KG-consistency. On Short Answer Feedback (SAF), KG-SoftMAP+VE reaches Fail-class F1 0.75 versus 0.78 for logistic regression while also providing an inspectable concept graph, calibrated Fail probabilities, and posterior queries from partially observed concept evidence. The remaining datasets sharpen the operating picture: weak heuristic KG signal leaves prediction unchanged, while an independent expert ontology moves the learned graph toward expert relatedness.
comment: 12 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables; includes a 24-page technical supplement

title: Dynamic Execution Horizon Prediction for Chunk-based Robot Policies
summary: Action chunking has become a standard design in modern robot policies, from diffusion/flow policies to vision-language-action models, where the policy predicts a sequence of actions and executes a fixed number of them instead of acting one step at a time. However, this paradigm relies on a key assumption: a fixed execution horizon. During chunk execution, the policy operates open-loop, which is particularly problematic for fine-grained manipulation tasks that require frequent replanning. In practice, the execution horizon is typically chosen through empirical tuning and is highly task-dependent. To this end, we propose Dynamic Execution Horizon Prediction (DEHP), an effective method that trains a lightweight execution-horizon prediction branch using online reinforcement learning while keeping the pretrained chunk policy completely frozen. This makes the method compatible with black-box chunk policies and isolates the effect of adapting the execution horizon from changes to the underlying action generator. Across our evaluations, DEHP improves the success rate of different high-precision and long-horizon manipulation tasks by a large margin. Our qualitative analysis further shows that DEHP predicts shorter execution horizons during fine-grained stages of the task and longer horizons during free-space motion. In this way, DEHP balances the efficiency of open-loop chunk execution with the reactivity of closed-loop single-step control. Project page: https://dehp-chunking.github.io/

title: Bridging Modal Isolation in Interleaved Thinking: Supervising Modality Transitions via Stepwise Reinforcement
summary: Interleaved thinking, where a unified multimodal model alternates between textual reasoning and visual generation, has shown promise on spatial and physical tasks. However, in complex long-chain scenarios, we identify a fundamental failure mode: generated images diverge from the textual context while subsequent text ignores the visual evidence, causing the two modalities to alternate without genuinely informing each other. We term this Modal Isolation and attribute it to compounding information loss at modality boundaries. We decompose each reasoning cycle into atomic operations and define modality transition loss, quantifying cross-modal hallucination (text-to-image) and visual utilization deficit (image-to-text) at each boundary. We propose MoTiF (Modality Tiransition Fidelity), a two-stage training framework that directly optimizes these transitions: Reflective SFT trains the model to detect and recover from erroneous visual outputs; Flow-GRPO improves image generation fidelity via reinforcement learning. All training signals in MoTiF derive from transition-level fidelity rather than end-task accuracy. Across four visual puzzle benchmarks, this transition-level supervision substantially improves both cross-modal coherence and final task accuracy. The results demonstrate that effective interleaved reasoning requires explicit structural supervision at modality boundaries, not merely scaling or end-task optimization.

title: Selective Mask Propagation for Multi-Object Tracking
summary: In multi-object tracking, most frames are easy for a lightweight base tracker while a small fraction is intrinsically hard. Video object segmentation (VOS) models can often preserve identity through the hard frames where the base tracker fails, but they are much more expensive in compute and memory. We propose selective mask propagation, a tracking algorithm that dispatches from a base tracker to a VOS model only on windows where an assignment-uncertainty signal fires. The base tracker's output is modified only when the VOS model makes a confident prediction that contradicts the base tracker's identity assignment; weak or inconclusive predictions preserve the base output. The method is training-free, treats both the base tracker and the VOS model as black boxes, and can benefit from replacing the VOS component with a more capable model. On DanceTrack, selective mask propagation significantly improves three different base trackers. On SportsMOT, where identity preservation is central to sports analytics, SAM 3-Deep-EIoU with global track association achieves state-of-the-art performance on the benchmark with 87.2 HOTA.

title: uringscope: Portable, Low-Overhead Observability for io_uring
summary: io_uring moves I/O submission and completion into shared-memory rings. This makes it fast, and it also makes it invisible. strace sees only the ring setup, and the kernel tracepoints that expose the request flow are not stable ABI, so the few tools built on them work only on narrow kernel ranges. We present uringscope, a single-binary, language-agnostic observability tool for io_uring built on CO-RE (Compile Once, Run Everywhere) eBPF. uringscope makes four contributions. The first is a precise model of the request lifecycle and a method to reconstruct per-request flows from kernel events. The second is a technique for attaching portably to an unstable tracepoint surface, using BTF-probed program variants, CO-RE field flavors, and position-independent reads. The third is an evaluation of the tradeoff between overhead and fidelity: on device-bound NVMe workloads uringscope's aggregate mode costs 0.7 to 9.9% of throughput, which is cheaper than every full-fidelity alternative we measured. The fourth is a lightweight correctness mode that reuses the same reconstruction to detect submission-boundary hazards, together with a built-in doctor that turns the measurements into named pathologies with evidence, for operators who are debugging a tail-latency incident rather than browsing histograms.

title: Sub Terahertz LEO Satellite Communication: Vision, Opportunities, and Challenges toward the First Prototype in Space
comments: 6 Pages, 5 Figures, 1 Tables. The work has been submitted to IEEE Wireless Communications Magazine
summary: The landscape of sub-terahertz (sub-THz, 100GHz - 300GHz) wireless technology evolved drastically over the last two decades - from only a few niche use cases in sensing and ultra-short-range communications in early 2000s toward operational multi-kilometer range 100GBbit/s+ wireless backhaul links demonstrated recently. Building on this momentum, this article explores the feasibility of extending sub-THz communications to 100-km-scale satellite links. We first assess the technological readiness of emerging sub-THz hardware and signal-processing techniques, highlighting their potential to support long-range operation in low-Earth-orbit (LEO) systems. We then outline the unique role that sub-THz links can play as a complementary solution to existing millimeter-wave and optical (``laser'') satellite technologies, offering additional capacity, improved resilience, and new architectural flexibility. We further discuss open research and engineering challenges toward implementing such sub-THz satellite communication systems in practice. We finally outline the key state-of-the-art solutions and the roadmap of TeraLink, an ongoing international R&D project aiming to build and launch, through an approved NASA CSLI space mission, the first hardware prototype of sub-THz LEO satellite communications in space.
comment: 6 Pages, 5 Figures, 1 Tables. The work has been submitted to IEEE Wireless Communications Magazine

title: OmniOPSD: Rationale-Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation for Affective Computing
summary: Reinforcement learning for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) is often hindered by severe reward sparsity in complex reasoning tasks. This challenge is particularly pronounced in human-centered scenarios involving states, emotions, intentions, and behaviors, where heterogeneous multimodal signals and subjective human factors make high-quality chain-of-thought (CoT) annotations expensive and difficult to obtain. Although many multimodal datasets provide expert-annotated ground-truth labels, directly using these labels for supervised fine-tuning may encourage shortcut learning in multimodal perception and provides limited transparency for safety-critical human--AI interaction. To address these limitations, we propose OmniOPSD, a Rationale-Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation framework that uses frontier-generated rationales as teacher-side privileged evidence rather than student imitation targets. OmniOPSD uses frontier-generated evidence-aware rationales only as training-time privileged evidence context for a local teacher. The student samples its own rollout from the original multimodal input, while the rationale-privileged teacher scores the same tokens and provides dense token-level supervision. Thus, the student learns on its own trajectory distribution without directly imitating frontier-model completions, and inference requires no labels, rationales, CoT annotations, or closed-source model access. Experiments on MER-UniBench show that OmniOPSD achieves state-of-the-art performance with an average score of $84.19$, and ablations further support the value of rationale-privileged teacher guidance.

title: LiteOdyssey: A Lightweight Reasoning AI Agent for Interpretable Rare-Disease Diagnosis
summary: Rare disease diagnosis involves interpreting clinical and genetic findings through complex diagnostic reasoning. We investigated whether this reasoning could be translated into a portable policy for guiding general-purpose large language models (LLMs) without modifying model weights or requiring resource-intensive infrastructure. We developed liteOdyssey, a lightweight framework built through Policy Iteration with Human Feedback (PIHF), in which clinicians review the model's reasoning process to iteratively update the policy. This policy guides evidence gathering, tool use, and differential diagnosis generation with an auditable reasoning process. In an external evaluation of 515 Undiagnosed Diseases Network patients, liteOdyssey improved diagnostic accuracy over general-purpose LLMs. These results suggest a strategy for medical AI in which expert reasoning is operationalized as an auditable, reusable policy layer that guides unmodified LLMs without resource-intensive infrastructure.

title: Training and Evaluating Diffusion Policies with Long Context Lengths
summary: Imitation learning has enabled highly-dexterous robotic manipulation from RGB observations. Policies trained with these methods, however, typically condition robot actions on only a short history of observations. These policies cannot solve tasks that require memory and can get stuck repeatedly executing the same failing motions. In this work, we first benchmark policy performance as context length is incrementally increased from short to long, across a spectrum of tasks with varying local stability and memory requirements, and in multiple data regimes. To our knowledge, this is the first study to investigate context length for Diffusion Policies at this level of detail. Our results challenge prior claims: naively scaling context length is not as brittle as advertised in literature. With an appropriate conditioning method and denoising backbone (UNet+Cross-Attention), single-task policies achieve high success rates on many tasks in the usual data regime even with naive scaling. Next, we propose a training algorithm to jointly train policies at multiple context lengths, further reducing the sample complexity of long-context learning. Finally, we apply our findings to re-evaluate some previously proposed solutions to long-context imitation learning.

title: TNODEV: Toolbox for Neural ODE Verification
comments: 30 pages, 7 figures, Under review in TMLR
summary: Neural ordinary differential equations (neural ODE) gained attention in safety critical settings such as continuous-time controllers for cyber-physical systems and classifiers integrated into automated decision pipelines, raising the question whether their behavior can be formally verified. Existing tools dedicated to neural ODE provide only a single reachability call without iterative input-set refinement, limiting the precision of their verdicts to whatever one reachability call can deliver. We present TNODEV, the first formal verifier for neural ODE that integrates a falsification checker, a fast interval-based reachability backend based on continuous-time mixed monotonicity, a verification and refinement loop with three input-set splitting heuristics, and a parallel scheduler in a single end-to-end pipeline. TNODEV supports safe-set inclusion verification on pure neural ODE, neural ODE in closed loop with a neural network controller and general neural ODE (GNODE), with the safe set specified either as an interval or as the half-space intersection induced by a target classification label. We evaluate TNODEV on a range of benchmarks across safe-set inclusion and classification-robustness properties, including a direct reachability comparison against NNV 2.0 and CORA and a verification comparison against NNV 2.0 on MNIST general neural ODE classifiers.
comment: 30 pages, 7 figures, Under review in TMLR

title: DRIFT: Risk-Constrained Diffusion with Imitation Priors for Mixed-Autonomy Traffic Generation
summary: Future intelligent transportation systems are envisioned to evolve toward a long-term mixed-autonomy paradigm, where human-driven vehicles (HVs) and autonomous vehicles (AVs) coexist within highly coupled traffic ecosystems. Such coexistence introduces pronounced heterogeneity, amplified uncertainty, and increasingly intricate interaction dynamics. In this context, it remains fundamentally challenging to simultaneously capture the heterogeneous behavioral distribution shifts arising from dynamic AV penetration, generate diverse yet executable trajectories under strong inter-vehicle coupling, and conduct reliable closed-loop safety and stability diagnostics for rare but high-impact events. To this end, we present Diffusion with Risk constraints, Imitation priors, and long-tail Feedback for mixed-autonomy Traffic generation (DRIFT), a mixed-autonomy traffic generation framework that unifies heterogeneity-aware conditional encoding, conditional diffusion-based executable trajectory generation, and progressive adversarial alignment enhanced by risk-aware long-tail feedback, thereby enabling traffic behaviors to be iteratively generated, filtered, selected, and validated within a closed-loop execution pipeline. In addition, a unified evaluation protocol is developed to jointly characterize safety, efficiency, and closed-loop stability across representative traffic scenarios and AV penetration regimes. Experimental results demonstrate that DRIFT achieves a strong safety-efficiency trade-off in closed-loop mixed-autonomy benchmarks, while further revealing the critical influence of candidate executability, online selection, and long-tail feedback on executable traffic evolution.

title: Diagnosing Shape-Prior Shortcuts in Long-Range Single-Shot Fringe Projection Profilometry
summary: Learning-based single-shot fringe projection profilometry (FPP) has been studied almost entirely at close range, and the networks used are evaluated only on aggregate error, leaving open whether they recover depth from fringe phase or from object-level shape cues that correlate with depth. This paper diagnoses that question mechanistically in the long-range regime (standoff beyond 1 m). Using FPP-ML-Bench, an open photorealistic synthetic benchmark (15,600 fringe images, 50 objects at 1.5--2.1 m), we first formalize why the single-shot fringe-to-depth mapping is more severely ill-posed at long range: it is non-injective without fringe-order information, and the depth error from an incorrect fringe order grows as $Z^2$ in the working distance. Systematic ablations, extended with a multi-frame study, establish a best UNet baseline at 14.54 mm object mean absolute error (MAE), 18% of the 80 mm object depth range, with only a 1.9$\times$ spread across four architectures, indicating a representational rather than a capacity-bound limit. A mechanistic interpretability study, the first applied to an FPP network, localizes the cause: linear probing shows edges are 2.82$\times$ more decodable than depth, Grad-CAM shows attention favoring boundaries over fringes by 1.28$\times$, and an in-range flat-plane test collapses a featureless plane to background depth despite valid fringes. The baseline solves the task via object-boundary shape priors rather than fringe-phase decoding. Because the shortcut is a hypothesis-space property, additional data or larger models will not remove it, motivating an architectural repair that removes the shape-prior solution by construction.

title: SPHINX: First Explain, Then Explore
summary: Generating adversarial driving scenarios is critical for evaluating and improving autonomous vehicle decision-making systems in simulation. Recent approaches rely primarily on the prior knowledge of Large Language Models and Vision-Language Models to generate driving scenarios procedurally. We argue that adversarial scenes should be generated based on the failure diagnosis (e.g., indecisiveness, multi-frame inconsistency) of the driving policy to specifically address the policy's weaknesses instead of relying on prior assumptions. In this paper, we propose SPHINX, a closed-loop framework for adversarial scenario synthesis guided by a simple principle: first explain, then explore. Beyond blindly exploring the scenario space, SPHINX leverages explainable artificial intelligence methods to analyze the policy, identifying key visual concepts and their influence on policy outputs, and the uncertainty of the decisions. Given the interpretable evidence extracted from the policy's own decision process, we use a vision language model to rationalize and criticize failure modes of the current policy. These critics are then used to generate targeted adversarial scenarios for policy retraining and improvement. We demonstrate that SPHINX can highlight an interpretable account of policy failures while other adversarial scene generation cannot. Across the evaluated benchmarks and test suites, SPHINX can be applied to diverse state-of-the-art autonomous vehicle architectures and yields consistent robustness improvements over existing scenario-generation methods.

title: Counterexamples to Wegner's Conjecture for Rectangles
summary:
Wegner conjectured in 1965 that every finite family $\mathcal R$ of axis-parallel rectangles satisfies $τ(\mathcal R)\le 2ν(\mathcal R)-1$, where $τ(\mathcal R)$ is the minimum number of piercing points and $ν(\mathcal R)$ is the maximum size of a pairwise-disjoint subfamily. We disprove the conjecture by an explicit triangle-free family of $64$ rectangles with $ν=16$ and $τ\ge 32$.
  More generally, for every $\varepsilon>0$, we construct triangle-free rectangle families for which the standard clique-LP relaxation for maximum independent set of rectangles has integrality gap at least $5/2-\varepsilon$. The same families satisfy $τ(\mathcal R)\ge (5/2-\varepsilon)ν(\mathcal R)$. We also prove that, on triangle-free rectangle families, this LP has gap at most $3$. Our approach gives an example with axis-parallel segments instead of rectangles with integrality gap tending to $2$. We also give a relatively small $4092$-rectangle triangle-free family with chromatic number $6$ improving the construction of Asplund and Grünbaum (On a coloring problem, Mathematica Scandinavica, 1960) that required more than $10^8$ rectangles.

title: Auto-correlation Function Keying
comments: 25 pages, 15 figures, submitted to IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
summary:
We propose ACFK: Auto-correlation Function Keying, a new integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) waveform that carries random communication data while directly controlling the peak sidelobe level (PSL) of the periodic auto-correlation function (P-ACF). In contrast to existing works aiming at controlling the expected sidelobe level (ESL), which fails to characterize realization-specific sidelobe behaviors, we formulate a mutual information maximization problem under PSL and power constraints, and show that a continuous ACF-domain uniform distribution is asymptotically optimal at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) over quasi-static frequency-flat channels.
  Motivated by this principle, ACFK maps finite-constellation symbols onto auto-correlation function (ACF)-domain sidelobes and uses independent phase symbols to exploit the remaining degrees of freedom. The resulting waveform enables exact control of the nominal P-ACF, which coincides with the actual P-ACF when the power spectral non-negativity condition is satisfied. We further analyze the non-negativity violation probability and bound the corresponding peak sidelobe level ratio (PSLR) degradation. A reference ISAC transceiver and its high-SNR approximate bit error rate (BER) analysis are also provided. Numerical results show that ACFK achieves stronger PSLR control, and improved weak-target detection performance, than a generalized probabilistic amplitude shaping (PAS) baseline at similar data rate and BER.
comment: 25 pages, 15 figures, submitted to IEEE Transactions on Information Theory

title: Hierarchical Control in Multi-Agent Games: LLM-based Planning and RL Execution
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved strong performance in sequential decision-making, yet scaling to complex multi-agent environments remains challenging due to sparse rewards, large state-action spaces, and the difficulty of learning coordinated strategies. We propose a hierarchical architecture where a pretrained large language model (LLM) acts as a centralized strategic controller that selects among specialized RL skill policies for a team of agents, while RL policies handle reactive low-level execution. We evaluate this hybrid system in a competitive 2v2 King of the Hill environment against behavior tree (BT) and \emph{``Flat''} RL (end-to-end training without skill decomposition) baselines. The LLM+RL system achieves task performance statistically equivalent to hand-crafted BT (46.4\% vs 51.5\% win rate, $p=0.103$) while both significantly outperform Flat RL trained without skill decomposition.
